messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: 3xx->5xx spike on /v1/generate EU region seen at 2028-11-03T09:05:21Z, latency > 5s — oncall @eu needed

jordan: seeing same, spike started ~09:04 UTC. traffic routed to eu-west-1->model-quantized-v1 fallback pool. errors look like backend timeout / kv-cache miss cascade.

maya: confirmed 5xxs and high latency in traces. Smart-routing logs show repeated fallback decisions cycling between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 for same client IP prefixes.

samir: paging @oncall, taking this. quick check: are DNS records for edge vip stale? I see some old rrsets in the edge cache.

jordan: dig from a few locations:
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood.example @1.1.1.1
34.210.12.11
34.210.12.11
```
but from eu-central vantage:
```
$ dig +short edge.redwood.example @8.8.8.8
34.210.99.77
```
which is an older rrset we retired last week.

alex: that mismatch explains route churn. Smart router uses DNS-based geo-weights then falls back to model-variant policy when endpoint mismatch occurs. If one region still resolves to old IPs it triggers repeated fallback.

samir: timeline: DNS change rolled Friday to move traffic off eu-old->eu-new. TTL was 300, but we've seen intermittent prop delays. Provider reports some authoritative caches holding older rrset. Triggered our routing policy which tries region, then fallback to any-compatible-region which oscillates.

incident-bot: New annotation: impact=partial degraded, customers_affected=[smith-analytics, quickcart-prod, voxai-sandbox], error_rate_peak=18%

maya: mitigation plan: 1) stop smart-routing fallbacks for affected model family (disable fallback flag) 2) purge edge DNS caches where possible 3) engage DNS provider to force reprop

jordan: executing step 1 now — toggling policy:
```
PATCH /api/config/routing/policies/geo_fallback
{ "enable_fallback": false, "notes": "temp disable to stop oscillation - 1867504321" }
```
response: 200 OK. fallback disabled.

samir: good. step 2: purging CDN edge cache & DNS at the edge nodes we control. run: `edgectl cache purge --host edge.redwood.example --regions eu-*`

alex: triggering DNS provider force-push, pinged dns-provider-sre in parallel.

dns-provider-sre: we see some stale parents due to a handful of misbehaving resolvers holding long-lived negative cache entries. We pushed a zone refresh and requested purge from our upstream peers. Should see propagation in 2-6 minutes for most peers.

maya: monitoring traces — error rate dropped from 18% -> 4% within 90s of disabling fallback. latency back to baseline for most flows. still seeing a handful of clients hitting old IP (34.210.99.77).

jordan: confirming: removed old A records from edge-tier yesterday but some authoritative caches still answered old rrset. We need to add scrubbing rule in smart-router to ignore endpoints outside the allowed active pool for 10m while we heal.

samir: putting temporary scrub rule: `route_policy.ignore_unregistered_endpoints=true` for 10m. Applied.

alex: starting customer comms draft: short status to affected accounts, note limited impact and mitigation steps. Maya can you own comms?

maya: I got it. drafting now — cc @success.

incident-bot: Note: automated rollback protection prevented an automatic canary-promote to quantized v2 in eu-west-1 during the window. That likely avoided bigger error blast.

jordan: post-mitigation verification: run synthetic jobs across EU nodes and confirm consistency:
```
for ip in $(cat eu-nodes.txt); do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SYNTH" https://$ip/health | jq .; done
```
all returned healthy: true across eu nodes.

samir: handoff to morning oncall @alex in 30m. leaving notes: 1) fallback disabled (manual) 2) scrub rule active until 09:40 UTC 3) DNS provider rep confirms propagation 4) follow-up: add guard that smart-routing should prefer verified active endpoints not just DNS answer.

alex: taking handoff. I'll keep scrub rule for another 15m and then revert if clean. Also will open a ticket to add endpoint verification in routing decision (owner: eng-runtime).

maya: customer impact summary for notes: 3 enterprise customers saw elevated 5xxs and latency for ~3 minutes, no data loss, some requests retried. Visibility: alerts triggered and oncall paged within 60s.

jordan: RCA notes (initial): root cause = stale authoritative DNS rrset + routing policy that permits fallback to any-compatible-region leading to oscillation. Contributing: DNS cache retention on some upstream resolvers + no endpoint verification in smart-router.

samir: follow-ups (owners):
- eng-runtime: implement endpoint verification in decision flow (owner: jordan)
- infra: add DNS propagation checks to zone-deploy playbook (owner: maya)
- sre: add metric for route-oscillation detection (owner: samir)
- support: customer comms and postmortem (owner: maya)

incident-bot: Incident severity set to SEV3. ticket=INC-2028-1447 assigned.

alex: reverting manual changes in 40m after clean verification. leaving note in runbook. great job team. :thumbsup:

maya: will publish postmortem draft by EOD.

samir: thanks all — closing live channel, moving to postmortem thread.
